newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen staying flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen staying flat.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell in lower turnover on Thursday but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main index up and analysts said the market should extend its flat trend to the Christmas holiday.
"We could have a slight rise, but there should be no big (main index) movements in prices or turnover in the pre-holiday period," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Some analysts said the market could rise after the holiday, in part in anticipation of better first-quarter earnings.
Others said the central bank head's comments that interest rates could rise if fast credit growth continues could help cool market sentiment in January.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.2 percent to 13,851.9 points and turnover fell 6.6 percent to 101.1 million zlotys ($35.4 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 42 to 27 with 13 stocks flat.
Analysts said Thursday's biggest losers, garment maker Bytom and construction firm Remak, fell 9.9 and nine percent after the two firms posted losses in November.
They said Bytom was also hurt by the bourse's approval for trade of 250,000 Bytom shares sold at 27 zlotys ($9.4) in an undersubscribed public offering.
They said top gainer furniture maker Swarzedz, up 9.7 percent with strong buying after price fixing, was helped by gaining a 200-million-mark contract.
Continuous trade turnover was at 7.7 million zlotys ($2.7 million) with six stocks up, one down and four flat.
NFI units rose 0.4 percent to 138.5 zlotys ($46.5) and rose 6.6 percent to 146 zlotys ($51.1) in 29.6-million-zloty ($10.4 million) continuous trade.
